generation: Generate PerformanceConfig numeric constants from parameters. Existing FlightProfiles 19-field generation remains unchanged.

policy.units: Original UnitType.speed converted to tiles/second by caller; hitSize to tiles; maxHealth is a dimensionless gameplay input, never asserted to be kilograms. Physics uses the existing metersPerTile conversion.
policy.mass: Unit mass scale = clamped(size/reference)^2 * (finite health/reference)^healthExponent, bounded by MIN/MAX_MASS_SCALE. Physical gameplay mass = original base mass * unit mass scale * user mass modifier; size bounded separately. Independent unit base-mass lookup is available for ram targets.
policy.agility: Finite nonnegative native speed enters a fractional power, then the derived agility and practical speed scales are bounded. Agility decreases with mass and rises with native speed; affects turn rates, response, thrust reserve and reference acceleration cap. Principal inertia scales with mass and size squared. Original unit AI/type stats are never modified.
policy.heavyMobility: From 0.5, burden=min(HEAVY_MAX_BURDEN,max(1,massProxy/HEAVY_MASS_THRESHOLD)^HEAVY_MASS_EXPONENT * max(1,sizeScale/HEAVY_SIZE_THRESHOLD)^HEAVY_SIZE_EXPONENT). Divide the former practical-speed scale by burden and the pre-clamped agility by burden^HEAVY_AGILITY_EXPONENT. This continuously reduces large-unit speed, acceleration reserve and torque/rates while retaining mass, principal inertia and the hover reserve. Units below both thresholds retain their previous behavior.
policy.nativeIdentity: UnitMetadata includes the exact native UnitType.name; its legacy four-argument constructor means unknown identity. Only the exact base-game name flare receives FLARE_SPEED_MULTIPLIER on the aerodynamic reference, after generic unit scaling and before the 400m/s cap. Its real speed/size/health, mass, inertia, thrust and rates remain unchanged. This is the user's explicit unit-specific tuning; other units/mod-prefixed names do not inherit it. The multiplier applies to every preset/custom profile, but Insane may reach the existing cap before a full 1.5x gain.
policy.thrust: Unit motor force derives from native size/mass/agility then power modifier. User mass reduces acceleration without automatically granting more motor force. Reference acceleration cap scales by unit agility with a minimum hover reserve; cannot create more force than available motors.
policy.drag: Practical speed is an aerodynamic reference, not instantaneous velocity clipping. Unit speed scale and drag modifier derive a bounded target <=400m/s. Linear and quadratic drag coefficients are calibrated to that target at full sustained level-flight thrust. Gravity/impulses/dives can overshoot. Unpowered/underpowered profiles have no sustainable level-flight speed.
policy.response: Motor and angular-rate response time constants are bounded and preserve fixed250Hz integration. Rigid-body state and motor spool are preserved on profile changes; same scale/timestep required.
policy.settings: Preset index0 Cinematic,1 Freestyle(default),2 Race,3 Insane,4 Custom. Custom values are explicit bounded sliders and retain existing saved pitch/roll/yaw/expo. Presets also respect user base rates, multiplying by preset and native-unit agility. Rebuild only on metadata/settings change.
policy.limits: Original aggregate force/torque model remains; no claim of four-rotor simulation or Liftoff physics. No hard scalar speed assignment. High-speed collision remains caller responsibility and requires real integrated sweep testing.
policy.flightSpeed: Flight speed25..300% applies to all presets after unit scaling, before400m/s bound. Recalibrate drag continuously; do not reset pose/inertia or change native UnitType. Build precision speed is separate.

acceptance: Legacy controller tests unchanged; physical profile swap preserves pose, velocities, motor response and fractional step
Freestyle materially faster than legacy; Race and Insane faster again with reference target <=400m/s
Same preset makes small/fast unit lighter, quicker and more agile than huge/slow unit
Named Flare measures about 1.5x its identical unnamed 0.4 reference in Cinematic/Freestyle/Race, retains physical metadata/force/inertia, and respects the Insane cap
Antumbra/Eclipse generic mobility falls progressively below 0.4, with measured sustained speeds matching new references; medium units stay unchanged
Mass/power/drag/response/acceleration/rates custom settings independently affect resolved behavior
No instant velocity clamp when changing settings; finite extreme metadata and bounded custom settings
Pure simulated sustained speed and timestep consistency, plus separate native high-speed collision smoke required
